We have 20 points labeled 1 through 20 arranged on a circle. We draw line segments between pairs of points whose labels differ by a prime number. We want to find the number of triangles formed whose vertices are among these 20 points and whose edges are all drawn (i.e., all three pairs of vertices differ by a prime number).

Step 1: Identify the prime differences possible between labels 1 to 20.

The possible prime differences are primes less than 20:
2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19

Step 2: Construct the graph.

Vertices: 1 to 20

Edges: between vertices i and j if |i - j| is in {2,3,5,7,11,13,17,19}

Note: Since the points are on a circle, the difference is taken modulo 20, but the problem states labels differ by a prime number, so the difference is the absolute difference of labels, not the circular distance. So edges are between points whose labels differ by a prime number in the usual integer sense.

Step 3: Find all triangles in this graph.

A triangle is a set of three vertices {a,b,c} such that all three edges (a,b), (b,c), and (a,c) exist.

Step 4: Approach to count triangles.

- Vertices: 1 to 20

- Edges: between i and j if |i-j| ∈ P, where P = {2,3,5,7,11,13,17,19}

We want to find the number of triangles in this graph.

Step 5: Since the graph is symmetric and the edges depend only on the difference of labels, the graph is a circulant graph with connection set P.

A circulant graph on n vertices with connection set S has edges between vertex i and i+s mod n for each s in S.

But here, the difference is absolute difference, not modulo n. So the edges are between i and j if |i-j| ∈ P.

Since the labels are from 1 to 20, the difference is just |i-j|, no modulo.
